citation.title: Experimental behavior of FRP strengthened masonry arches

document.fullTextVersion: repository copy of the published paper (ASCE)
document.accessNote: Full text retrieved from the University of Minho repository on 2026-08-16. Tables 1 and 2 of the paper are not readable from the retrieved copy; the per-specimen peak loads are therefore taken from the authors' PhD thesis record basilio-2007-thesis, which is the same campaign's primary dataset.
document.license: repository open access; paper copyright ASCE

abstract: This paper deals with the experimental behavior of solid clay brick masonry arches strengthened with glass fiber reinforced polymer composites. Twelve half-scaled segmental masonry arches subjected to a load applied at the quarter span were tested under displacement control up to failure. (...) only continuous strengthening strategies are able to prevent typical local failure mechanisms of unreinforced arches; (2) strengthening at the intrados is the most effective option to increase strength; (3) strengthening applied at the extrados provides the higher deformation capacity prior to failure.

extractionNotes: Full text of the published paper retrieved from the University of Minho repository (hdl.handle.net/1822/17430) on 2026-08-16.

Paper Tables 1 and 2 are not readable in the repository copy; per-specimen peak loads are taken from the authors' PhD thesis (Basilio 2007, hdl.handle.net/1822/8124, Table 6.5), which is the primary dataset of the same campaign. Every such value is marked with its thesis location.
Unit weight, friction angle, and cohesion were not found in the extracted text and are recorded as UNKNOWN.
Displacements at peak load are available only through the published load-displacement figures; digitization is planned and must be marked approximate-digitized with stated tolerance.
Hinge angular positions are available only from Figure 5a of the paper.
